bug_functions: components/prism-javascript.js//'keyword' token pattern (the regex in Prism.languages.javascript['keyword'])
1.explanation: The core of the problem is the `keyword` token in the JavaScript grammar (defined in components/prism-javascript.js). Its regex uses word boundaries (`\b`) to match keywords like `from`, but doesn’t exclude cases where the keyword is part of an identifier beginning with `$`. As a result, in `$from`, the `from` segment satisfies the pattern and is highlighted as a keyword. To fix this, the `keyword` regex must be adjusted (e.g. refine the lookbehind to treat `$` as part of an identifier) so that keywords are only matched when they are standalone and not embedded in variable names like `$from`.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting JavaScript code that destructures properties whose names include a keyword, e.g. const { $from, $to } = selection;, Prism’s JS grammar misclassifies the “from” part of “$from” as a reserved keyword. In the screenshot, $from is rendered with keyword styling even though it’s an identifier.

2.explanation: The root of the problem is in the JavaScript grammar definition inside components/prism-javascript.js (and its minified counterpart). The ‘keyword’ token includes a regex that matches reserved words such as “from” and “to” when they appear at word boundaries. Because the pattern’s lookbehind allows any non-word character (including “$”) before the keyword, “$from” is split into “$” + “from”, and “from” is then erroneously classified as a keyword. To fix this, the keyword regex in Prism.languages.javascript['keyword'] must be refined to exclude the “$” character from its lookbehind, so that dollar‐prefixed identifiers are not broken apart and misrecognized as keywords.
2.bug_scenario: In the code snippet “const { $from, $to } = selection;” the identifiers “$from” and “$to” are being highlighted as JavaScript keywords (in red) instead of as regular variables. In the screenshot you can see that the dollar‐prefixed names are marked as keywords, even though only “from” and “to” appear in the Prism “keyword” regex list—Prism’s tokenizer is splitting “$from” at the “$” and then matching “from” as a keyword.
